items.item: The schedule and drawings agree on zones, areas, inventory, storage allocations and the public and staff arrangement.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Read the drawings together using the southwest internal floor corner as origin, x east, y north and z upward. Verify D1 at south-wall x=0.8–2.0 m, 2.4 m high, west-hinged and outward opening; W1 at south-wall x=2.6–7.4 m with sill z=0.45 m and head z=2.7 m; full-height C1 at x=3.8–4.2, y=5.8–6.2 m; and full-height SH1 at x=7.4–8.0, y=9.4–10.0 m. E1 and E2 remain on the east wall at y=7.5 and 8.8 m, z=0.45 m; WP1 remains there at y=9.4 m, z=0.5 m. Annotations may establish positions and heights that a particular projection cannot show. Missing evidence of service retention, relocated elements or contradictory geometry fails.

Identify four distinct sale rails with 1200 × 500 mm footprints and 1600 mm height, two sewing tables measuring 1200 × 600 × 750 mm, and one pressing table measuring 1200 × 600 × 900 mm. Rail allocations provide twelve garments per rail, forty-eight total. Labels or a keyed equipment record may establish heights and capacities. Sewing machines remain associated with the two sewing tables and pressing has its own table; substituted counts, incompatible footprints or missing retained equipment fails.

The application sheet explicitly associates FL-01 with the retained floor and honed matte terrazzo, WD-01 with reclaimed oak and clear matte varnish on counter facing and new joinery, PT-01 with opaque-wall limewash specified as #D8CCBA, and AC-01 with suspended wool felt of 25 mm thickness above both sewing stations. Keyed annotations or a legend are acceptable. A swatch without its material, treatment and location is insufficient; contradictory or omitted specifications fail.

The early function schedule defines each zone's name, area and occupancy, garment capacities, equipment quantities and dimensions. Zone areas sum to 79.48 square metres with circulation included and the column and shaft excluded. Inventory includes four sale rails, two sewing stations, one pressing table and one fitting room. The presentation repeats the schedule's zone names, areas and counts without changing their meaning; omission, double-counted circulation or conflicting records fails.

The plan visibly uses the source schedule's zone names, area values and equipment counts, with drawn footprints supporting those allocations. Sewing and pressing are in the north half. Zone shapes may be design-dependent, but missing source fields, overlaps that invalidate the area allocation or a different inventory fails.

The image set preserves the 8 × 10 m room, 3.2 m clear height and fixed elements, including H1 at x=7.4–8.0, y=1.8–3.6 m with top z=0.9 m. The furnished plan dimensions actual narrowest customer routes at 1200 mm or more, unobstructed 1500 mm entrance and fitting-room circles, and a 2000 × 2200 mm clear fitting room. V1–V4 have position and direction markers. The east section labels counter, glazing, storage and ceiling heights. Projection differences are allowed; contradictory geometry, missing clearance evidence or furniture obstructing the stated spaces fails.

The circulation drawing distinguishes public customer movements from garment processing and identifies sale, waiting and completed allocations of 48, 12 and 8 garments. AR1 and RC1 are separate units with individually identified positions. Purchase connects entry, rails, optional fitting, counter and exit; garment processing connects H1, AR1, sewing, pressing as needed, RC1 and collection. Customers stay on the public side. The section establishes an upper glazed divider and unobstructed views from the customer side of H1 to both sewing surfaces. Arrow styles and storage arrangement may vary; conflated streams, missing stages or obstructed visibility fails.

The plan provides daily and Saturday occupancy diagrams with one sales assistant and two makers in each. Daily customers comprise one browsing and one collecting; Saturday comprises three browsing, one fitting, one repair handover and one collecting. V1 and V3 carry Saturday captions specifying six customers and three staff; V2 and V4 carry daily captions specifying two customers and three staff. Visible activity agrees with the caption, and furniture remains in the same positions across states. Off-camera occupants are allowed; inconsistent totals, roles or moved furniture fails.

The source sheet locates finishes, mounting positions and controls; section and ceiling representations agree with it. Felt panels are suspended above both sewing tables. The lighting record specifies ceiling linear L1 at 3000 K over sales and circulation, articulated L2 at 4000 K at both sewing tables and the pressing table, and adjustable track L3 at 3000 K above all four rails. Three independent circuits map to three switches on the staff side of H1. V2 has readable material callouts and each furniture detail has the codes relevant to its depicted assembly and surroundings. Symbol styles may vary; missing codes, wrong assignments or spatial disagreement fails.

The rail detail explains the retained 1200 × 500 × 1600 mm dark steel rail and placement of twelve garments on its single top bar. The workstation detail shows the 1200 × 600 × 750 mm sewing table, off-white machine, chair, pedal below, articulated task light and identifiable working clearance. Details agree with equipment on the plan. Drawing scale and annotation style may vary; missing required components, incompatible dimensions or an unexplained twelve-garment allocation fails.

Match each perspective to its furnished-plan camera: V1 (1.4,1.2) northeast toward Saturday handover, V2 (6.7,5.0) north toward daily repair, V3 (1.0,5.0) northeast toward the Saturday fitting approach, and V4 (5.8,2.6) east toward daily collection. All use a plausible 1.6 m eye level and include state occupancy captions. Lens and crop may vary while preserving camera origin, direction and subject; substituted viewpoints or missing subjects fail.

The plan locates the shop name above D1; V1 and V4 print it on the counter front. V1 places the sale label at a rail, and V2 makes the two repair-state labels legible on their respective stores. Styling may vary; page headings, floating captions or legends do not replace signage on the required objects.

The presentation has at least eight pages and prints the shop name on page one. It includes the three named garment stores with capacities 48, 12 and 8, both purchase and garment-processing sequences, and the source application's four material codes and three lighting codes with consistent meanings. A storyboard follows entry, browsing, H1 handover and a final workshop view. Page layout may vary; missing facts, contradictory source information or an absent route storyboard fails.

Every source role is visibly reused in the presentation as identifiable, readable content. Scaling, cropping and page composition are allowed when the relevant drawing or view remains recognizable. Merely listing filenames, substituting new contradictory drawings or omitting any source fails.

Review the complete video and its duration. It runs ten seconds, starts at D1, moves along the planned public route through browsing to H1, and ends looking into the workshop. The shell, openings, column, shaft, fixed counter and furniture layout remain compatible with the drawings throughout. Camera pacing and transitions may vary; entering the staff-only workshop, skipping a route stage, changing the layout or failing to show the workshop at the end fails.
